subnets.name: Compute Horde
subnets.description: computehorde is a specialized subnet (subnet 12) within the Bittensor network, designed to provide scalable, decentralized, and trusted GPU computing power for validators across other Bittensor subnets. By transforming untrusted GPUs from miners into reliable compute resources, computehorde reduces dependency on centralized services and enables cost-effective, large-scale validation. Key features include fair and verified work mechanisms, scalable mining with multiple executors per miner, hardware class-based resource allocation, a developer SDK for easy integration, collateral-based trust for organic jobs, and an optional DDoS shield for miners. The project aims to support a wide range of GPU types and offers a robust scoring and incentive system to ensure quality and accountability.

subnets.description: Thinker is a reasoning-model subnet where participants (miners) submit LoRA adapters designed to enhance a fixed base model's performance on math, long-context question answering, and multiple-choice reasoning tasks. Validators evaluate these adapters for reasoning quality, efficiency, and compactness, rewarding those that improve performance without increasing resource demands. The system emphasizes repeatable evaluation, strict answer formatting, and fairness through deterministic shuffling and scoring. Submissions mature on-chain before evaluation, and the protocol supports integration with tools like Weights & Biases for live tracking. The project is tailored for efficient, scalable reasoning model improvements within a collaborative, on-chain environment.

subnets.name: ReadyAI
subnets.description: readyai is an open-source project that provides a low-cost, resource-efficient data structuring and semantic tagging pipeline for individuals and businesses. It transforms raw data into structured, AI-ready formats suitable for vector databases and AI applications. The system leverages distributed miners and validators, using large language models (LLMs) like OpenAI's GPT-4o to annotate and tag data. Validators establish ground truth and score miner submissions based on similarity metrics, ensuring data quality. The platform is designed for scalability, incentivizing data contribution and validation through a mining and rewards mechanism.

subnets.name: BitMind
subnets.description: Gas (Generative Adversarial Subnet) is a Bittensor subnet designed to advance AI-generated media detection and synthesis through open, incentivized competition. Inspired by generative adversarial networks, it features two parallel tracks: discriminative mining, where participants submit models to detect synthetic images, videos, and audio, and generative mining, where participants generate convincing synthetic media. Validators orchestrate challenges and scoring, ensuring continuous evolution of both detection and generation capabilities. The system leverages cloud-based evaluation, supports multiple modalities, and refreshes datasets weekly to stay ahead of emerging synthetic content threats.

subnets.description: Eirel is a decentralized execution layer for multimodal AI workflows, operating as a Bittensor subnet (subnet 36). It enables users to turn a single prompt into a shipped product by orchestrating competing AI agents across language, vision, audio, and code. The platform supports autonomous planning, code generation, media creation, data extraction, and tool integration, all coordinated through a transparent, on-chain incentive system. Eirel splits roles between miners (who submit and run AI agents) and validators (who score agent outputs), rewarding high-quality contributions with TAO emissions. The roadmap includes expanding specialist agent families and progressing toward full decentralization, aiming to create an open, competitive network for real-world AI-powered workflows.

Unlike traditional GANs, dojo v2 challenges miners to produce outputs that are not only indistinguishable from high-quality baselines but also superior, creating a dynamic environment where participants act as both generators and discriminators. Miners can easily participate without running servers by registering and using a browser wallet, while validators help maintain network integrity. The project emphasizes ease of entry, competitive AI advancement, and decentralized participation.

Greevils provides a CLI for packaging, submitting, and deploying trading agents, with strict on-chain ownership verification and incentive alignment through emissions. The project aims to benchmark and incentivize the development of superior trading agents in a transparent, high-stakes environment.

Babelbit targets critical industries and use cases where instant, natural multilingual communication is essential, positioning itself as a disruptive solution in the $100 billion language services market.
